coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep covering six leading graph database engines (Neo4j, TigerGraph, Memgraph, ArangoDB, Kuzu, FalkorDB) across all major evidence axes: official product surfaces (homepages, pricing, docs, changelogs), primary funding records (Tracxn, PitchBook, Crunchbase, CB Insights), user-generated review aggregates (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Gartner Peer Insights), analyst reports (Gartner, Forrester), competitive comparison teardowns, HCI pain points (learning curve, UI complexity, RAG/knowledge-graph adoption friction), performance benchmarks, market forecasts, and community sentiment (Hacker News, Knowledge Graph Conference). Deduplication applied across vendor-published comparisons vs. third-party reviews. Tier assignment: T0 (live product pages, SEC/funding records), T1 (official docs/changelogs/API), T2 (G2/Capterra/analyst reports), T3 (vendor comparison blogs, HN discussions, practitioner guides). License notes distinguish between public product pages (reference-only), open documentation (redistribute-ok for OSS projects), proprietary analyst PDFs (reference-only), and GitHub-hosted code (open-source license). Notable coverage: (1) Kuzu acquisition by Apple documented via multiple sources; LadybugDB community fork tracked; (2) FalkorDB's GraphBLAS sparse matrix design covered via technical blogs + GitHub README; (3) GraphRAG/RAG pain points surfaced through multiple 2026 practical guides; (4) GQL standardization (ISO/IEC 39075:2024) and Cypher convergence documented; (5) Neo4j's GraphAware acquisition (June 2026) documented. Gaps/deferrals: specific G2/Capterra rating counts require direct page fetch; Ultipa competitive standing mentioned but fewer detailed sources; ArcadeDB coverage solid but emerging alternative; some analyst reports (Gartner Market Guide PDF) require subscription access.
